record.context: The interior order imposes a 12-hour election-day frontier closure. It is recorded as a distinct legal measure overlapping SC17 COVID policy; the government announced land and river COVID reopening separately on 28 February 2022. No additional non-overlapping duration is assigned.

followup_reviews.Research finding: Retain the distinct 2021 presidential-election closure order as included; a legal measure can be represented without proven operational enforcement. The official order covers national borders, with the land/river component retained. The separate adjacent domestic vehicle order supplies no border exemptions. Direction and actual affected cohort remain unobserved. Retain 21 March 2021 from 06:00 to 18:00 as twelve ordered hours, with no whole-day operational duration. Expiry is neither observed reopening nor repeal of other restrictions; the 2022 COVID reopening announcement is a distinct policy event. Retain Electoral politics / Election administration and security from the explicit electoral purpose. The separate COVID policy is relationship context, not an additional rationale for this order. The official gazette directly supports order 4500. The freshly read February 2022 government statement supports the separate COVID policy announcement, but neither establishes all-post operations during March 2021. Retain unlocated national land/river-order scope and null coordinates. No border post or continuous geometry is inferred from the national legal wording.
